content: {"summary":"To safely reduce a Kafka topic's retention, the runbook advises checking consumer lag, cleanup policy, per‑partition retention settings, segment state, and disk usage before making the change.","likely_cause":"N/A","confidence":"medium","claims":[{"text":"Check consumer lag before shortening retention","evidence_ids":["RB-009#2"],"quote":"Check consumers before you shorten anything."},{"text":"Ensure the topic is not using a compacted cleanup policy","evidence_ids":["RB-009#5"],"quote":"Compacted topics ignore this."},{"text":"Remember retention.bytes applies per partition, not per topic","evidence_ids":["RB-009#5"],"quote":"`retention.bytes` is per partition, not per topic."},{"text":"Only closed segments are removed; active segment may retain data","evidence_ids":["RB-009#5"],"quote":"Retention only removes closed segments."},{"text":"Identify the biggest topics and confirm broker disk usage","evidence_ids":["RB-009#1"],"quote":"Find the biggest topics."},{"text":"Monitor broker retention cleanup timing after the change","evidence_ids":["RB-009#3"],"quote":"The broker checks retention every 5 minutes by default"}],"next_checks":["Run kafka-consumer-groups.sh to view the largest LAG for the target topic","Describe the topic and verify cleanup.policy is not set to compact","Check the topic's retention.bytes setting and calculate per‑partition impact","Inspect segment.ms and segment.bytes to understand active segment size","Run df -h /data/kafka on each broker to see current disk usage","Watch df output for 10‑15 minutes after the change to confirm cleanup"]}
